content: 1. ATP7A is a Cu2+-transporting ATPase, also known as alpha polypeptide (EC: 3.6.3.4), involved in copper export. Its human gene ID is 540. 2. ATP7B is a Cu2+-transporting ATPase, also referred to as beta polypeptide (EC: 3.6.3.4), responsible for copper export. Its human gene ID is 540. 3. A zinc-translocating P-type ATPase catalyzes the reaction: ATP + H2O + Zn2+(in) → ADP + orthophosphate (Pi) + Zn2+(out). This enzyme can also export Cd2+ and Co2+. It requires Mg2+ as a cofactor. 4. A proton-translocating P-type ATPase generates an electrochemical proton gradient across the plasma membrane by catalyzing the reaction: ATP + H2O + H+(in) → ADP + orthophosphate (Pi) + H+(out). It requires Mg2+ as a cofactor. 5. A sodium-translocating P-type ATPase facilitates the reaction: ATP + H2O + Na+(in) → ADP + orthophosphate (Pi) + Na+(out). It requires Mg2+ as a cofactor. 6. Calcium-translocating P-type ATPases catalyze the reaction: ATP + H2O + Ca2+(cis) → ADP + orthophosphate (Pi) + Ca2+(trans). There are three types: one in the plasma membrane, one in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, and one in the sarcoplasmic reticulum. The first two transport one ion per ATP hydrolyzed, while the third transports two ions. Human gene ID: 487. 7. ATP2A1 is a sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum calcium ATPase (SERCA) found in cardiac muscle, fast-twitch fibers. It translocates calcium (Ca2+) from the cytosol to the sarcoplasmic reticulum lumen. Human gene ID: 488. 8. ATP2A2 is a SERCA calcium ATPase found in cardiac muscle, slow-twitch fibers. It performs the same function as ATP2A1. Human gene ID: 489. 9. ATP2A3 is a ubiquitous SERCA calcium ATPase that translocates calcium ions. Human gene ID: 490. 10. ATP2B1 is a plasma membrane calcium ATPase (PMCA) that transports calcium ions. Human gene ID: 491. 11. ATP2B2 is another PMCA calcium ATPase, specific to plasma membrane transport. Human gene ID: 492. 12. ATP2B3 is a PMCA calcium ATPase found in the plasma membrane. Human gene ID: 493. 13. ATP2B4 is a PMCA calcium ATPase located in the plasma membrane. Human gene ID: 9914. 14. ATP2C2 is a type 2C calcium-transporting ATPase. Human gene ID: 23400. 15. A sodium/potassium-transporting ATPase catalyzes the reaction: ATP + H2O + Na+(in) + K+(out) → ADP + orthophosphate (Pi) + Na+(out) + K+(in). This enzyme, found in the plasma membrane of animal cells, exchanges three Na+ ions for two K+ ions per ATP hydrolyzed, generating the plasma membrane electrical potential. 22.
